wesleyTravels.title: The Travels of John Wesley
wesleyTravels.subtitle: 400,000 km traveled mainly on horseback — the equivalent of going around the Earth 10 times. Wesley had no cathedral: the whole of Britain was his parish.

statistics.label: Age at death — active until the end

places.name: Newcastle upon Tyne
places.note: First major breakthrough in the North (1742). Wesley founded Orphan House there — his first major charitable institution.

places.name: Leeds
places.note: Center for Industrial Methodism. Wesley holds several annual conferences there.

places.name: Bristol
places.note: Cradle of Methodism (1739). First open-air preaching at Kingswood. The New Room — the first Methodist chapel.

places.name: Epworth (Lincolnshire)
places.note: Hometown of John and Charles. Wesley preaches there at his father's grave after being refused entry into the church.

regions.visits: 22 trips to Scotland, 43 trips to Ireland

places.name: Edinburgh
places.note: First trip in 1751. Wesley preached there before thousands of people despite the initial hostility of the Presbyterians.

places.name: Dublin
places.note: Center for Irish Methodism. Wesley made 43 voyages there — crossing the Irish Sea at the age of 80.

places.name: Cork
places.note: Scene from the violent anti-Methodist riots of 1749. Wesley courageously returned there the following year.

regions.visits: 32 trips to Cornwall, the main ground for evangelization

places.name: Redruth (Cornwall)
places.note: Capital of Cornish Methodism. Tens of thousands of miners converted. The Methodist societies of Cornwall are among the strongest.

places.name: St Ives
places.note: First breakthrough in Cornwall (1743). Wesley goes down into the mines to preach to the miners after work.

places.name: Cardiff
places.note: Gateway to Methodism in Wales, difficult but fertile ground.

places.name: Savannah, Georgia
places.note: Base of the American mission of Wesley (1736-1737). Pastor of a colonial parish. Difficult mission, complicated relationships.

places.name: Frederica (Georgia)
places.note: Place of a violent pastoral conflict which precipitated the departure of Wesley. He returns to England convinced that he has not yet found the true faith.

journal.label: 📔 Journal of John Wesley
journal.quote: "At 4 a.m. set out for Epworth. At 6 a.m. preached in a field to about 200 people despite wind and rain. At 10 a.m. arrived in Newcastle where I preached again. At 3 p.m. rode to Durham..."
journal.attribution: — Typical extract from Wesley's journal, July 1757
